hints.title: Signed Thirty-Two Bit Overflow Bound
hints.text: Reversing digits mathematically requires popping the last digit and appending it to the result. How can checking thirty-two bit limits prevent integer overflow before multiplying by ten?

hints.title: Pre-Multiplication Overflow Invariant
hints.text: Multiplying by 10 will overflow if the running reversed value is already greater than 214748364.

hints.title: Digit Extraction and Overflow Check Procedure
hints.text: Extract sign of x. Work with absolute value of x. While x is greater than zero: take digit = x % 10, check if rev > (2^31 - 1) // 10, update rev = rev * 10 + digit, and divide x by 10. Reapply sign and verify within signed 32-bit bounds, returning 0 if overflow occurs.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def reverse(self, x: int) -> int:
        sign = -1 if x < 0 else 1
        x = abs(x)
        rev = 0
        limit = (1 << 31) - 1
        while x > 0:
            digit = x % 10
            x //= 10
            if rev > (limit - digit) // 10:
                return 0
            rev = rev * 10 + digit
        ans = sign * rev
        return ans if -(1 << 31) <= ans <= limit else 0
```

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(log N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Converting to string and parsing may still overflow 32-bit signed integer types in statically typed languages like C++ or Java.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Iterative decimal digit extraction completes in at most 10 iterations with O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle the sign, prevent 32-bit integer overflow, and return 0 on overflow.
